output.decision: Do not launch one broad multivariate test across hero, offer, and checkout this month. The site’s 600,000 monthly sessions are likely sufficient for meaningful testing, but testing three funnel areas at once will make attribution, interaction effects, checkout exposure, and required sample size difficult to manage. Instead, use this month to define evidence-backed hypotheses and launch one or more non-conflicting, adequately powered tests—starting with the highest-priority change.
next_steps: Analyze funnel drop-off, device, traffic-source, customer-type, and post-purchase/support feedback to identify friction behind each proposed change.
Write separate hypotheses for hero, offer, and checkout, including the expected revenue-per-session effect and rationale.
Estimate sample size and test duration for each variant combination using checkout-entry volume, not total site sessions; predefine primary and guardrail metrics.

Prioritize ideas by expected impact, visibility, implementation effort, and evidence; launch the top isolated test first, or test separated funnel areas only if allocation and attribution remain clear.
QA randomization, pricing/offer logic, checkout behavior, analytics events, and revenue tracking before launch; run through at least two weekly cycles and avoid overlapping changes to the same page.
missing_inputs: Proposed hero, offer, and checkout variants, including the number of combinations and traffic allocation plan.
Checkout-entry and purchase volumes by device and major traffic source.
Historical revenue per session, average order value, refund/cancellation rate, and acceptable downside thresholds.
Research evidence for each change, such as survey responses, session recordings, funnel diagnostics, or support themes.

evidence_used.supports: The supplied source recommends multivariate testing only at high volume, clear data-backed hypotheses, 50k–100k sessions per test, two-to-four-week durations, QA, avoidance of conflicting tests, and prioritizing revenue over conversion rate.

assumptions: Tracking validation means experiment assignment, purchases, and revenue can be measured reliably.
The stated 600,000 monthly sessions are sitewide; usable traffic for checkout tests may be materially lower.
This recommendation treats the supplied library as unverified guidance rather than independently validated fact.
No urgent promotional, platform, or checkout-release deadline requires bundling all three changes this month.
